what_happened: Live repo-wide dry run of RV_BLOCKING_ERE/RV_ADVISORY_ERE (scripts/lib/record-version-patterns.sh) against both this repo and the Logos/Verification repo (the acceptance-test target) found 251 and 213 BLOCKING hits respectively, not the 0 the acceptance criterion requires. Root cause isolated: RV_PAGE_LABEL_ERE's heading-form branch (^#{1,6}[[:space:]].*\bv[0-9]+\b) fires on any line starting with 1-6 '#' chars containing a bare vN token ANYWHERE later in the line, with no requirement that the token denote the PAGE'S OWN draft version. This conflates markdown ATX headings with shell/code '#' comment lines using unrelated V-numbered internal labels (git-commit-scoped.sh: 75 hits, its test: 70, orchestrate-batch-admit.sh: 23), and also fires on legitimate headings naming an EXTERNAL entity's real version (Tailwind v4, a schema's own 'Global Index Schema (v2)', a decision-numbering convention like '(v6 Ruling)'). The library's own calibration note (record-version-exemptions.md) states it was calibrated only against the Verification repo's docs/, README.md, books/, and records/ trees -- never against .sh files or other extensions' markdown, which is exactly where the false positives concentrate. Separately confirmed: the pattern library's own test fixture file (test-record-version-patterns.sh) embeds literal unmarked BLOCKING/ADVISORY strings as test data (10 hits), needing the same task-ref-ok-style marker treatment test-check-task-references.sh already uses for an identical self-reference problem. Also confirmed real (likely genuine) un-swept positives: lua/neotex himalaya plugin docs ARCHITECTURE_V2.md/DRAFT_SYSTEM_V2.md carry literal page-level version-labeled titles. Full detail and file-by-file evidence in the research report.

Re-derived the research report's dry-run at plan-authoring time (251/731 here, 213/757 Verification, all reproduced) AND measured a candidate two-discriminator narrowing that drops BLOCKING to 27/19, so the plan could budget library-fix phases with a real residue target instead of a guess.

Planning-time discovery not in the research report: strip_durable_axis_lines and strip_exempt_regions DELETE lines, so a downstream grep -n reports post-strip line numbers. Measured drift confirmed (reported 610 vs real 611; 549 vs 550). Sibling check-task-references.sh has the same latent defect via strip_exempt_regions; out of this task's file scope, noted for a follow-up.

The research report identified only tests/test-record-version-patterns.sh as self-flagging. Measurement found two more: rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md (2 findings) and context/standards/record-version-exemptions.md (1), both of which necessarily quote the forbidden vocabulary. Plan Phase 4 widened to cover all three.

Worked around for in-dispatch verification via a scratch copy of the test file with LIB_CANDIDATES pointed at the source-store path only; the real test file and its deploy-tree-first resolution were left untouched. All 45 assertions (38 pre-existing + 7 new Phase 2 fixtures) pass against the source-store library.

Direct ad hoc 'source lib; grep ...' debugging in this dispatch's own interactive Bash-tool shell silently used a shadowing 'grep' shell function (ugrep -G compatibility layer) instead of real GNU grep, and ugrep's engine gave WRONG verdicts for this library's \b...\b.{0,80}\b...\b proximity patterns (false negatives) even though the library's own header explicitly warns 'the actual runtime engine is always GNU grep, not the ugrep shell-function substitution ... never pasted into an agent's own top-level Bash-tool shell'. Caught by a contradiction between a direct-source debug check (false negative) and a bash-subprocess-based probe (correct positive) on the same file/line. All load-bearing verification in this dispatch (the fixture suite and the corpus probes) was run via 'bash scriptfile.sh', a genuine subprocess that does not inherit the interactive shell's grep function, so those results are unaffected -- only my own supplementary ad hoc debugging was affected, and was discarded once the discrepancy surfaced.

class: logic defect, caught before deliverable landed
what_happened: rv_grep_blocking's non-markdown branch (added in Phase 2) always returned exit 0 (sort's own exit status) regardless of whether any line actually matched, silently breaking the grep-compatible 0=found/1=not-found contract for a direct caller checking its exit status. Caught via a sanity check during Phase 4 (rc=0 with empty output, a contradiction under grep's own contract) before any consumer script depended on it. Fixed: the non-markdown branch now captures the merged/sorted result and returns 0 only when non-empty, 1 otherwise. Two regression assertions added to test-record-version-patterns.sh.

check-record-versioning.sh's LIB_CANDIDATES (modeled on check-task-references.sh's sibling convention) prefers the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/lib/record-version-patterns.sh over the source-store copy, even under a REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) source-store invocation override -- that override only bypasses deploy-root-guard.sh's REPO_ROOT computation, not library resolution order. Running the real script against this repo's own stale deployed core (Phases 1-4 not yet redeployed) reported 240 BLOCKING instead of the correct 5, matching the OLD pre-Phase-2 library behavior. Verified the script's own logic is correct by temporarily moving the stale deployed library aside, re-running (got exactly 5, matching the independent probe), and restoring the original file byte-identical (diff -q confirmed). This is the same deploy/source-store staleness trap already logged for test-record-version-patterns.sh's deploy-tree-first library resolution, now confirmed to affect the real deliverable script too, not just the test harness. No action taken on this repo's own deployed core per the dispatch's explicit instruction not to force a workaround; the next cycle's redeploy checkpoint resolves it for both consumers.

class: logic defect, caught before acceptance claim landed
what_happened: During Phase 8's own Verification-repo acceptance verification, discovered check-record-versioning.sh silently reported a FALSE PASS (0 BLOCKING, 0 ADVISORY, exit 0) against the Verification repo's own deployed library, which predates even this task's Phase 1 work entirely (186 lines, no rv_grep_blocking/rv_grep_advisory/rv_is_markdown_path functions at all). Calling an undefined rv_grep_blocking inside a pipeline whose stderr the script redirects to /dev/null produces exit 127 with no stdout, so the scan loop silently never iterates -- a stale/incompatible library was indistinguishable from a genuinely clean repo. Fixed: after sourcing the library, check-record-versioning.sh now verifies all five required functions (is_exempt_path, strip_durable_axis_lines, strip_exempt_regions, rv_grep_blocking, rv_grep_advisory) are actually defined via 'declare -F', exiting 2 with an actionable message naming the missing function if not -- the same environment-error severity already given to a library not found at all. Added a regression case (Case 14) to test-check-record-versioning.sh using a deliberately stale stand-in library. Re-ran the Verification-repo acceptance checks with the FIXED source-store library temporarily substituted for the test (restored byte-identical immediately after, diff -q confirmed): named-files sub-claim genuinely passes (0 BLOCKING each); repo-wide sub-claim genuinely fails (exit 1, 14 BLOCKING, all inside Verification's own deployed .claude/ copies of this repo's three self-referential files plus the two Phase-8 judgment-call lines) -- exactly the already-anticipated deploy-staleness gap, now confirmed for real rather than masked by the false-pass defect.
